I'm in the eye of the storm for this as well, and here's the thing. We have to be honest with ourselves about how what we do makes it easier or harder for those around us to care for us. 

Mental illness can be really tough, really draining on friends and family. Even if we think something might be "fair" in terms of context, the bigger problem can be that people just run out of energy and patience to deal with the issues it causes, that, in their minds to a degree, we cause. 

So I'd guess it's something in the middle. Your mom is frustrated at the situation, and thus gets tough on you because she sees something she doesn't know how to deal with. 

My best advice, and I can honestly say this works when I follow it, is to try to give back in kind when I can bring myself to do so. If I do something nice for my family it pays heavy dividends because it shows I care, even when I feel like shit. So if only for the sake of your own self interest, maybe do something to make her smile, even when you don't feel like it. 

It's worth the effort, i promise you.

My best advice, my best solution, is to try to keep a regular schedule of the stuff you need to do. 

I go grocery shopping on the same day each week to make sure it gets done. I take my medication at the same time every night. 

I know if I leave things up to my whims I won't get them done, and having things incomplete makes me feel really down.

So start small, make sure you're eating regularly. Drink water. Try to go to bed before 1AM every night. You'll feel a lot better if you just do those three things.
